title: Zutty's uncle Willie Bontemps and clarinetist Jimmie Noone
summary: Russell asks about Zutty and Jimmie Noone; Cottrell knows Noone only by records and a 1937 meeting.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: band until they had this. Well by the way, um, speaking of Willie Bontag, I can't pronounce those French names, but Zutty, I used to know him quite well in New York. That's his nephew. And he used to tell me about his uncle, and so when I ran across him on the parade, I recognized the name as soon as I was introduced to the course. Didn't get to talk to him in a half a minute, of course. In those days I didn't, wasn't studying the history as much as I am now. Yeah, nah, yeah. But I was thinking about Zutty. Did he ever study with your father? Do you remember anything about him? I can remember Zutty, but as for taking this night, I don't remember. No, I don't recall. Um, or you mentioned Jimmy Newton. Do you remember much about him here? I don't. Have you ever heard him or anything?

Oh, I remember seeing pictures of Jimmy and hearing recordings of Jimmy. And I did meet Jimmy in Chicago, although that was back in 1937. But other than that, I didn't know too much other than what I hear.

You don't know where he learned, who he studied? No, I don't. I really don't. Because the reason why I ask is that he seems to have something in common with your style and Omosimeon's style. I wondered if he was a T.O. student too.

I couldn't say. I really don't know. I talked to him a little bit when we wrote the book Jazzman, which is pretty much out of date, but we didn't have any tape recorders to remember what they said. I'd have a few notes on it when I talked in 1938. He was a wonderful clarinetist. Yes, he was. He really was.
During that period, it was great. He didn't mention then.
He might have told me. Maybe I can look up my notes. I really could say.
